stem: For solving the simultaneous equations \(x + y = 3\), \(3x - 2y = 4\). Find the value of determinant \(D\).
solution:
**(C)** \(-5\)

The determinant is formed from the coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\): \(D = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = (1)(-2) - (1)(3) = -2 - 3\). \(\therefore D = -5\).

stem: One of the roots of equation \(x^2 + mx - 5 = 0\) is 2, find the value of \(m\).
solution:
**(C)** \(\frac{1}{2}\)

Since 2 is a root, it satisfies the equation. Put \(x = 2\): \(2^2 + 2m - 5 = 0\), so \(4 + 2m - 5 = 0\), giving \(2m = 1\). \(\therefore m = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Check: \(4 + 2\times\dfrac{1}{2} - 5 = 4 + 1 - 5 = 0\).

solution:

Brokerage is a charge for a service given by the share broker, and GST on brokerage is levied at the rate of \(18\%\).

stem: The classification of persons based on blood groups is to be shown by a pie diagram. The persons having blood group O are \(40\%\). What should be the measure of angle for the persons having O blood group?
solution:
**(D)** \(144^\circ\)

Measure of the central angle \(= \dfrac{\text{percentage}}{100}\times 360^\circ = \dfrac{40}{100}\times 360^\circ\). \(\therefore\) the angle for blood group O \(= 144^\circ\).

stem: If \(15x + 17y = 21\) and \(17x + 15y = 11\), then find the value of \(x + y\).
solution: Adding the two equations: \((15x + 17y) + (17x + 15y) = 21 + 11\), so \(32x + 32y = 32\). Dividing both sides by 32, \(\therefore x + y = 1\).

stem: Find the first term and common difference of the given A.P. \(5, 1, -3, -7, \ldots\)
solution: First term \(a = t_1 = 5\). Common difference \(d = t_2 - t_1 = 1 - 5 = -4\). Check: \(t_3 - t_2 = -3 - 1 = -4\). \(\therefore a = 5,\ d = -4\).

stem: Two coins are tossed simultaneously. Write the sample space \((S)\) and the number of sample points \(n(S)\).
solution: Each coin shows Head (H) or Tail (T). Sample space \(S = \{HH, HT, TH, TT\}\). \(\therefore n(S) = 4\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem: Find Mean \((\bar{X})\) if \(\sum x_i f_i = 1265\) and \(\sum f_i = 50\).
solution: Mean \(\bar{X} = \dfrac{\sum x_i f_i}{\sum f_i} = \dfrac{1265}{50}\). \(\therefore \bar{X} = 25.3\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem:
Complete the following table by writing suitable numbers and words.

| Sr. No. | FV | Share is at | MV |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) | \(\text{₹}\,100\) | Par | \(\text{₹}\) |
| (2) | \(\text{₹}\) | Premium \(\text{₹}\,500\) | \(\text{₹}\,575\) |
| (3) | \(\text{₹}\,10\) |  | \(\text{₹}\,5\) |
| (4) | \(\text{₹}\,300\) |  | \(\text{₹}\,310\) |
solution:
At par, MV \(=\) FV. At a premium, MV \(=\) FV \(+\) premium. If MV \(<\) FV the share is at a discount, and if MV \(>\) FV it is at a premium.
(1) At par: MV \(= \text{₹}\,100\).
(2) FV \(= 575 - 500 = \text{₹}\,75\).
(3) MV is less than FV by \(10 - 5 = \text{₹}\,5\): Discount \(\text{₹}\,5\).
(4) MV is more than FV by \(310 - 300 = \text{₹}\,10\): Premium \(\text{₹}\,10\).

stem: Complete the following activity to find the probability of getting tail when one coin is tossed.
solution: Let \(S\) be the sample space. \(S = \{H, T\}\), so \(n(S) = 2\). Let A be the event of getting tail. \(A = \{T\}\), \(\therefore n(A) = 1\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)}\), \(\therefore P(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(5x + 3y = 9\); \(2x - 3y = 12\).
Form the quadratic equation whose roots are 3 and \(-10\).
solution: Let \(\alpha = 3\) and \(\beta = -10\). Sum of roots \(\alpha + \beta = 3 + (-10) = -7\). Product of roots \(\alpha\beta = 3\times(-10) = -30\). The required equation is \(x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0\), i.e. \(x^2 - (-7)x + (-30) = 0\). \(\therefore x^2 + 7x - 30 = 0\). Check: \((x + 10)(x - 3) = x^2 + 7x - 30\).

stem: 'Pawan Medical' supplies medicines. On some medicines the rate of GST is \(12\%\), then what is the rate of CGST and SGST?
solution: GST is divided equally between the Centre (CGST) and the State (SGST). Rate of CGST \(=\) rate of SGST \(= \dfrac{12\%}{2}\). \(\therefore\) rate of CGST \(= 6\%\) and rate of SGST \(= 6\%\).

stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by factorisation method: \(25m^2 = 9\).
If one die is rolled, then write the sample space \((S)\), \(n(S)\), event A in the set form and \(n(A)\). Event A: getting odd number on the upper face.
solution: Sample space \(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\). Event A: odd number on the upper face, \(A = \{1, 3, 5\}\). \(\therefore n(A) = 3\).

stem: M/s. Jay Chemicals purchased a liquid soap having taxable value \(\text{₹}\,8{,}000\) and sold it to the consumers for the taxable value \(\text{₹}\,10{,}000\). Rate of GST is \(18\%\). Complete the activity to find the CGST and SGST payable by M/s. Jay Chemicals.
solution:
Input tax \(= 18\%\) of \(8000 = \dfrac{18}{100}\times 8000 = \text{₹}\,1440\). \(\therefore\) ITC \(= \text{₹}\,1440\).
Output tax \(= 18\%\) of \(10{,}000 = \dfrac{18}{100}\times 10000 = \text{₹}\,1800\).
\(\therefore\) GST payable \(=\) Output tax \(-\) ITC \(= 1800 - 1440 = \text{₹}\,360\).
\(\therefore\) Payable CGST \(= \dfrac{360}{2} = \text{₹}\,180\) and payable SGST \(= \text{₹}\,180\) by M/s. Jay Chemicals.
Check: \(18\%\) of the value added \((10000 - 8000) = \dfrac{18}{100}\times 2000 = \text{₹}\,360\).

stem: Complete the following activity to find, 'how many three digit natural numbers which are divisible by 5'. Three digit natural numbers divisible by 5 are as follows: \(100, 105, 110, \ldots, 995\).
solution:
These numbers form an A.P. with \(t_n = 995\), \(a = 100\), \(d = 5\), \(n = ?\)
\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\) (formula)
\(995 = 100 + (n - 1)\times 5\)
\(895 = (n - 1)\times 5\)
\(\dfrac{895}{5} = n - 1\), so \(179 = n - 1\)
\(179 + 1 = n\)
\(\therefore n = 180\).
There are 180 three digit natural numbers divisible by 5. Check: \(t_{180} = 100 + 179\times 5 = 100 + 895 = 995\).

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by formula method: \(x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0\).
solution:
Comparing with \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \(a = 1,\ b = -3,\ c = -2\).
\(b^2 - 4ac = (-3)^2 - 4(1)(-2) = 9 + 8 = 17\).
\(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{-(-3) \pm \sqrt{17}}{2\times 1}\).
\(\therefore x = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{2}\) or \(x = \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{2}\).
Check: sum of the roots \(= \dfrac{6}{2} = 3 = -\dfrac{b}{a}\) and product \(= \dfrac{9 - 17}{4} = -2 = \dfrac{c}{a}\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
Electricity used by some families is shown in the following table. Find the mode of electricity used.

| Use of Electricity (Units) | No. of Families |
|---|---|
| 0–20 | 13 |
| 20–40 | 50 |
| 40–60 | 70 |
| 60–80 | 100 |
| 80–100 | 80 |
| 100–120 | 17 |
solution:
The highest frequency is 100, so the modal class is 60–80.
\(L = 60\), \(f_1 = 100\), \(f_0 = 70\) (frequency of the class before), \(f_2 = 80\) (frequency of the class after), \(h = 20\).
Mode \(= L + \left[\dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\right]\times h = 60 + \left[\dfrac{100 - 70}{2\times 100 - 70 - 80}\right]\times 20\)
\(= 60 + \dfrac{30}{50}\times 20 = 60 + 12\).
\(\therefore\) Mode \(= 72\) units. Check: 72 lies in the modal class 60–80.

The following table shows the classification of percentages of marks of students and the number of students. Draw a frequency polygon from the table.

| Result (Percentage) | No. of Students |
|---|---|
| 30–40 | 7 |
| 40–50 | 33 |
| 50–60 | 45 |
| 60–70 | 65 |
| 70–80 | 47 |
| 80–90 | 18 |
| 90–100 | 5 |
solution:
Find the class mark of each class, \(\dfrac{\text{lower limit} + \text{upper limit}}{2}\), and pair it with the frequency.

| Result (Percentage) | Class mark | No. of Students | Point |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30–40 | 35 | 7 | \((35, 7)\) |
| 40–50 | 45 | 33 | \((45, 33)\) |
| 50–60 | 55 | 45 | \((55, 45)\) |
| 60–70 | 65 | 65 | \((65, 65)\) |
| 70–80 | 75 | 47 | \((75, 47)\) |
| 80–90 | 85 | 18 | \((85, 18)\) |
| 90–100 | 95 | 5 | \((95, 5)\) |

Take the percentage of marks on the X-axis (scale: 1 cm \(= 10\) percent, with a break mark near the origin) and the number of students on the Y-axis (scale: 1 cm \(= 10\) students). Plot the seven points and join them in order with line segments. To close the polygon, take the class marks 25 and 105 of the classes 20–30 and 100–110 before and after the given classes, plot \((25, 0)\) and \((105, 0)\) on the X-axis, and join them to the first and last points. The closed figure is the required frequency polygon.

stem: The sum of the squares of five consecutive natural numbers is 1455. Find the numbers.

Ajay Sharma repays the borrowed amount of \(\text{₹}\,3{,}25{,}000\) by paying \(\text{₹}\,30{,}500\) in the first month and then decreases the payment by \(\text{₹}\,1{,}500\) every month. How long will it take to clear his amount?
solution:
The monthly payments \(30500, 29000, 27500, \ldots\) form an A.P. with \(a = 30500\), \(d = -1500\), \(S_n = 325000\), \(n = ?\)
\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2a + (n - 1)d\right]\)
\(325000 = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[61000 + (n - 1)(-1500)\right] = \dfrac{n}{2}\left[62500 - 1500n\right]\)
\(650000 = 62500n - 1500n^2\). Dividing by 500: \(1300 = 125n - 3n^2\), so \(3n^2 - 125n + 1300 = 0\).
\(3n^2 - 60n - 65n + 1300 = 0\), so \(3n(n - 20) - 65(n - 20) = 0\), giving \((n - 20)(3n - 65) = 0\).
\(n = 20\) or \(n = \dfrac{65}{3}\). The number of months must be a natural number, so \(n = 20\).
\(\therefore\) Ajay Sharma will take 20 months to clear the amount.
Check: \(S_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}\left[61000 + 19\times(-1500)\right] = 10\times 32500 = 325000\).

stem: If the point \((2, 1)\) lies on the graph of the equation \(x + ay = 4\), then find the value of \(a\) and draw the graph of the equation so obtained.
solution:
Since \((2, 1)\) lies on the graph, it satisfies the equation. Put \(x = 2,\ y = 1\): \(2 + a(1) = 4\). \(\therefore a = 2\).
The equation is \(x + 2y = 4\), i.e. \(y = \dfrac{4 - x}{2}\).

| \(x\) | 0 | 4 | 2 | \(-2\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 2 | 0 | 1 | 3 |
| \((x, y)\) | \((0, 2)\) | \((4, 0)\) | \((2, 1)\) | \((-2, 3)\) |

Plot these points on a graph paper (scale: 1 cm \(= 1\) unit on both axes) and join them. The straight line through them is the graph of \(x + 2y = 4\); it cuts the Y-axis at \((0, 2)\) and the X-axis at \((4, 0)\), and passes through \((2, 1)\).

stem: The following pie diagram represents the number of valid votes obtained by four students; who contested for school captain. The total of valid votes polled was 720. Answer the following questions: (a) Who has won the election? (b) What is the minimum number of votes? Who got it? (c) By how many votes did the winner defeat the nearest contestant?
solution:
Number of votes \(= \dfrac{\text{central angle}}{360^\circ}\times 720 = 2\times\) (central angle in degrees).
Ram: \(\dfrac{100}{360}\times 720 = 200\). Raj: \(\dfrac{80}{360}\times 720 = 160\). Shubha: \(\dfrac{120}{360}\times 720 = 240\). Radha: \(\dfrac{60}{360}\times 720 = 120\). Check: \(200 + 160 + 240 + 120 = 720\).
(a) Shubha has the largest central angle \((120^\circ)\), so Shubha won the election with 240 votes.
(b) The minimum number of votes is 120, obtained by Radha.
(c) The nearest contestant is Ram with 200 votes. \(\therefore\) Shubha defeated Ram by \(240 - 200 = 40\) votes.
